meta.thesis: tinyB's corporate-event engine reaches 82,000+ people a year but converts none of them to consumers - 'Borogodó, Delivered' bridges that gap into DTC gifting.
meta.variant_angle: rev1: activity matrix + thesis + itemized budget

business_problem: tinyB earns ~57% of revenue from corporate events - a capacity-limited channel - while consumer DTC gifting is only ~14% and wholesale ~7%. Its kits reach 82,000+ participants yearly but contain no path to a consumer purchase, so the brand's biggest audience never becomes its customer base.

objectives.text: Drive 1,000 new DTC orders during the 45-day Valentine's-anchored window
Grow the owned audience by 5,000 email/SMS subscribers and 10,000 campaign-attributed site sessions

segments.name: The Gifter - corporate attendees turned gift buyers
segments.demographic: 25-45, professionals who attended a tinyB corporate workshop (Google, Meta, Salesforce-type employees)

segments.psychographic: Experienced brigadeiros at a work event; associates the brand with a memorable hands-on moment; buys gifts for partners, friends, and hostesses

segments.media: Email (work-life), Instagram, word of mouth in office networks

segments.geographic: San Francisco Bay Area, then national

programs.name: The Corporate Bridge
programs.mechanic: Insert a 'Take Borogodó Home' card into every corporate event kit starting week 1: a QR code + 20% off first DTC order + a recipe card. 3,200+ annual events = the warmest audience the brand owns.

programs.name: Brigadeiro Bar
programs.mechanic: Weekend tasting bar at the San Mateo flagship plus 3 proposed Bay Area cafe partners: guests taste 3 brigadeiros, get a stamped card, and receive the gifting-box offer. Target 600 tastings.

programs.name: #ShareTheBorogodo
programs.mechanic: UGC challenge timed to Galentine's/Valentine's: post your gifting or tasting moment with #ShareTheBorogodo; weekly winners receive a brigadeiro box. All posts include #ad disclosure per FTC rules.

programs.name: Valentine's Brigadeiro Box
programs.mechanic: Limited-edition gift box (assorted brigadeiros + handwritten-style card + 'borogodó' meaning card) launched week 3 for Galentine's/Valentine's; promoted via email, SMS, and paid social to gift buyers.

programs.name: Renata's Kitchen
programs.mechanic: Founder-led content series: Renata Stoica shares the brigadeiro recipe origin story and 'borogodó' meaning weekly across TikTok and email; 6 food/lifestyle micro-creators seed the story weeks 1-3.

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: "Borogodó, Delivered: turn tinyB's 82,000 annual workshop attendees into customers." [S5]
Problem: ~57% of tinyB revenue comes from corporate events - a capacity-limited channel - while consumer DTC gifting is only ~14% [S5].
Business opportunity: kits reach 82,000+ participants yearly with no purchase path; Valentine's is a record $29.1B occasion where candy is the top gift [S2][S5].
Solution: 'Borogodó, Delivered' puts a consumer offer inside every corporate kit, samples at the flagship store, and launches a limited Valentine's Brigadeiro Box [O1].
45-day goal: 1,000 new DTC orders and 5,000 new email/SMS subscribers [O1][O2].

visual.desc: Four boxes: Problem / Business opportunity / Solution / 45-day goal

slides.notes: The key line: tinyB's best marketing already happens - inside corporate workshops - but it ends with a handshake, not a sale. We fix the last inch.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Handmade Brazilian brigadeiros - gluten-free bite-sized chocolates made in small batches in San Mateo [S5][S6].
Sold as singles, gift boxes, and experience kits; company average order ~$47 [S5].
Margins of 72-78% across channels - gifting and DTC carry the highest margins [S5].
4.8 Google / 5.0 Yelp ratings across 30,000+ customers served [S5].

visual.desc: Assorted brigadeiro flavors in brand packaging on marble

slides.notes: Brigadeiro is unknown in the US - that is the problem and the opportunity. A $29B chocolate category [S1] has never heard the word.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Founded 2014 by Renata Stoica, a Brazilian former nurse; ~40 employees; profitable and bootstrapped, raising $1.5M [S5][S7].
Revenue ~$916K in 2025, +30% YoY; mix: 57% corporate events, 22% store, 14% DTC gifting, 7% wholesale [S5].
Clients include Google, Cisco, Meta, Salesforce, PwC, Intuit - 3,200+ events in 52+ countries [S5].
Position: premium experiential chocolate - priced above mass-market, below luxury gifting [S5][S8].
slides.notes: This is a healthy, growing company - which is exactly why the pitch works: they do not need a rescue, they need a bridge from B2B love to consumer revenue.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary, conversion): 1,000 new DTC orders in 45 days [O1].
O2 (consideration): +5,000 email/SMS subscribers and 10,000 campaign site sessions [O2].
O3 (awareness): 3M impressions, 350K engagements, 250 #ShareTheBorogodo posts [O3].

visual.desc: O1-O3 rows with funnel stage, metric, target

slides.notes: Orders are the primary objective. Every program below ties back to O1, O2, or O3 - nothing runs on vibes.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1 'The Gifter': 25-45 professionals who already ate brigadeiros at a tinyB corporate event; buys gifts 2-4x/year; reachable by email and office word-of-mouth [S5][S8].
P2 'The Sweet-Seeker': 18-28 Gen-Z dessert loyalists; discovers food brands on TikTok; values gluten-free and founder stories [S4][S6].
Shared truth: edible gifts are the most-appreciated corporate gift (81%) and recipients are 79% more likely to remember the giver [S8].

visual.desc: Two persona cards with photos, demographics, psychographics, media habits

slides.notes: P1 is the unfair advantage - we are not buying this audience, the brand already taught them what a borogodó is. P2 is the growth audience.

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary research (complete): company investor brief, GlobalData, NRF, NCA, Circana/State of Treating, Giftsenda/Coresight [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S8].
Key results: US chocolate market $29.2B and growing 5.7%/yr [S1]; Valentine's hits a record $29.1B with candy the top gift [S2][S3]; 99.8% of households buy confectionery, avg $352/yr [S4].
Primary research (in field): 8-question survey of chocolate/gift buyers + 3-5 interviews with past corporate-event attendees; results load into slides 10 and 17 before submission [R-pending].
Environmental scan: cocoa prices and tariffs are squeezing chocolate COGS - making tinyB's asset-light gifting model (no grocery slotting) strategically attractive [S4].

visual.desc: Methods table + key stats bar chart (Valentine's $29.1B, chocolate $29.2B, household penetration 99.8%)

slides.notes: The chocolate category is huge but mature at 2.6% growth [S1] - tinyB's edge is not the category, it is the unclaimed brigadeiro niche and the owned audience.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: 57% of revenue sits in corporate events reaching 82,000+ people with no purchase path [S5] -> therefore every kit gets a 'Take Borogodó Home' card (G1).
Finding: Valentine's is a record $29.1B occasion; 92% hope to receive chocolate [S2][S3] -> therefore a limited Brigadeiro Box anchors weeks 3-6 (G4).
Finding: edible gifts are the most-appreciated corporate gift, 79% better recall [S8] -> therefore we pitch brigadeiros as the corporate-to-personal bridge.
Finding: 4.8 Google / 5.0 Yelp proof already exists [S5] -> therefore 'Renata's Kitchen' makes the founder the creative.
Finding (pending survey): gift-buyer price and channel data will re-weight spend in week 1 [R-pending].

visual.desc: Finding -> therefore rows (5), each tagged with source IDs

slides.notes: Same discipline as our other decks: every decision cites its evidence. The Corporate Bridge insight is the one that should make a judge lean forward.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea 'Borogodó, Delivered': the little extra that makes something special - tinyB's own word - now delivered from work event to home gift box.
IMC mix: Paid (TikTok/Meta) + Earned (founder story, PR) + Shared (UGC challenge) + Owned (kit inserts, email/SMS, POS).
Push-pull: corporate clients get a seamless gifting story (push); consumers get sampling, creator proof, and a limited box (pull); one QR code connects both.
Ownable element: only tinyB can put borogodó inside the kits it already runs - a competitor would have to buy an audience this brand already owns [S5].

visual.desc: Key visual: brigadeiro box with 'Borogodó, Delivered' lockup and the word's translation card

slides.notes: Theme check: 'Borogodó' appears on every activity slide. It is tinyB's own vocabulary - the campaign sounds like the brand, not like an agency.

slides.title: Program 1: The Corporate Bridge
bullets: Borogodó, Delivered starts inside the kits tinyB already ships: a 'Take Borogodó Home' card with QR code + 20% off first DTC order [O1][O2].
Mechanic: card goes into every corporate event kit from week 1; scan lands on a kit-specific page that captures email/SMS consent.
Why it works: 82,000+ participants already experienced the product - the warmest possible audience, at near-zero media cost [S5].
Measurement: per-kit QR codes attribute every order; target 800 scans and 150 redemptions [A5].

visual.desc: Insert card mockup: 'You just made borogodó at work - take it home. Scan for 20% off' + QR

slides.notes: This is the strategic centerpiece. Frame it as proposed: the client approves adding the card to kits - we are not claiming it already exists.

slides.title: Program 2: Brigadeiro Bar
bullets: Borogodó, Delivered goes sensory: weekend tasting bars at the San Mateo flagship and 3 proposed Bay Area cafe partners [O1][O2].
Mechanic: guests taste 3 brigadeiros, get a stamped loyalty card, and leave with the gifting-box offer and a QR code.
Target: 600 tastings over 5 weeks at ~$8 product cost each [A7].
Why it works: brigadeiro is unknown in the US [S6] - tasting converts curiosity faster than any ad.

visual.desc: Pop-up bar mockup: tasting cups, branded napkins, 'Borogodó, Delivered' banner

slides.notes: Sampling is the highest-trust channel for a novel food. The stamped card turns a one-time taste into a follow-up.

slides.title: Program 3: #ShareTheBorogodo + Valentine's Box
bullets: Borogodó, Delivered gets its moment: limited Valentine's Brigadeiro Box launches week 3 for Galentine's and Valentine's Day [O1].
UGC challenge: post your gifting or tasting moment with #ShareTheBorogodo; 5 weekly winners get a box; entries capture email/SMS [O2][O3].
Named decision-maker: founder Renata Stoica fronts 'Renata's Kitchen' - the brigadeiro origin story and what borogodó means [S5][S6].
6 food/lifestyle micro-creators seed the unboxing format weeks 1-3 so the challenge has examples on day one [O3].

visual.desc: Gift box mockup + TikTok phone frame showing unboxing with #ShareTheBorogodo caption

slides.notes: Valentine's timing is deliberate: record $29.1B spending [S2] and candy is the most-planned gift [S3] - the box gives the campaign a reason to exist now.

bullets: Email subject + preview: 'The little extra you just made at work - take it home' / '20% off your first borogodó box. Scan the card in your kit.' [O1][O2]
TikTok caption: 'POV: you finally learn what borogodó means (it's the best part). Valentine's box inside. #ShareTheBorogodo #ad' [O3]

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $19,000: media $6,500 [A4]; creators 6 x $700 = $4,200 [A6]; Brigadeiro Bar $3,000 + sampling $2,000 [A7]; insert cards $1,000 [A5]; email/SMS $800 [A9]; PR $300 [A10]; landing/QR $200 [A11]; contingency $1,000 [A12].
Funnel: 2.5M impressions x 1.2% CTR = 30K clicks x 4.5% conv = 1,350 orders x $47 AOV = $63K revenue [A1][A4].
GP at 72% margin = $45.7K; profit ROI 140%; ROAS 5.9x on $10.7K ad spend [A2].
Break-even 561 orders; base 1,350, conservative (50%) 675 - clears break-even [O1].
CAC $14.07 base / $28.15 conservative vs. $47 AOV at 72% margin [A1][A2].

visual.desc: Itemized budget table (9 lines with cost basis) + funnel math + base/conservative case

slides.notes: The insert card costs ~$1K and reaches 82,000 warm prospects - the cheapest reach in the plan. Lead with that ratio.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1 orders: Shopify + per-program QR/code attribution; target 1,000 orders; weekly review [O1].
O1 bridge metric: kit card scans and redemptions; target 800 scans / 150 redemptions [O1].
O2 list growth: Klaviyo/SMS dashboard; target +5,000 subscribers, 10,000 UTM sessions [O2].
O3 reach: Ads Manager + hashtag tracking; target 3M impressions, 350K engagements, 250 UGC posts [O3].
Optimization trigger: if kit-card scans < 200 by week 3, shift $1,000 from paid social to a second Brigadeiro Bar weekend; if UGC < 50 posts by week 4, add a creator prize boost [A4].

visual.desc: KPI table: objective -> KPI -> baseline -> target -> tool -> cadence

slides.notes: The kit-card scan metric is the one to highlight: it directly proves the corporate-to-consumer bridge works.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Thesis: "Borogodó, Delivered: turn tinyB's 82,000 annual workshop attendees into customers." [S5]
Mission metric: every brigadeiro carries 'borogodó' - the little extra; the campaign targets 1,000 new households discovering it [O1].
Founder thesis: Renata left nursing to share her mother's brigadeiro recipe with America - Borogodó, Delivered is how that story reaches the people who already loved the workshop [S6].
Projected result: $63K attributed revenue on a $19K budget; 675+ orders even in the conservative case [O1].
The lasting asset: a repeatable corporate-to-consumer bridge the brand can run for every holiday, not just Valentine's [O2].

visual.desc: Renata Stoica portrait-style image + 'Borogodó' lockup + projected results callouts

slides.notes: End where the strategy began: the brand does not need more awareness, it needs the last inch - from 'I loved that workshop' to 'I'll order the box.'
